quality.reason: The report content is well-structured with source URLs, engagement metrics, and signal scores, but leaked internal reasoning appears at the start of the output and entries like 'unknown→unknown' whale transfers are marginal signals, indicating room for improvement.

Well-structured operational summary with real fleet status, PnL metrics, and ranked signals, but signals lack direction or actionable parameters, contains a broken news link '[[]]', and duplicate ETH entries without deduplication limit its value.

Well-structured review with quantified metrics, clear margin/trend comparisons, and actionable flags (e.g., BTC's macd underperforming trend with declining score) that enable concrete strategy-switching decisions.

Well-structured alert with genuine signal — the ETH OI collapse (-9.6%/1h) combined with 78% ask-weighted orderbook is a real, quantified anomaly that traders could act on, and the prioritized alerts plus clean data table make it immediately scannable, though it slightly duplicates table data in the alerts and offers no interpretation of the liquidation dynamics.

Dense, well-structured digest with per-agent health deltas, flagged failures (meta-agent 47.4 ❌, x-scanner volume halved), and concrete remediation items (94+ files need archival, 2 stale sources with specific ages), making it clearly actionable rather than noise.

Well-structured digest with transparent methodology disclosure, verified paper IDs with links, and highly relevant papers (e.g., agentic trading cost analysis), though reliance on web-search fallback due to arXiv API rate limits slightly increases verification risk.
The output is a truncated fragment of raw markup syntax ('</arg_value>') with no readable findings, structure, or actionable signal from the research agent.

issues: Doc embeds machine-specific transient state in the Status line (install status of imsg/memo/remindctl, binary path /opt/homebrew/bin/imsg) which will go stale immediately and is wrong for any other machine — installation state belongs in a per-environment check, not the skill body
Verification date 2026-08-19 and the tool statuses cannot be independently confirmed from this excerpt; the doc should state how to re-verify (commands) rather than only asserting a past verification

All three tools (antoniorodr/memo, steipete/tap/remindctl, steipete/tap/imsg) are niche third-party taps with single maintainers — high abandonment/rename risk; no fallback (e.g., raw osascript/AppleScript equivalents) is documented if a tap dies

referenced/ docs (references/apple-notes.md, references/apple-reminders.md, and presumably references/imessage.md) are asserted present but not verifiable from this excerpt; a dead relative link would silently break the 'Full reference' pointers
AppleScript/automation-permission-based CLIs are fragile across macOS major updates (TCC permission resets, app bundle changes); doc lacks a note on re-granting permissions after macOS upgrades
Minor: content is truncated mid-section (iMessage permissions), so the remainder of the doc was not reviewable

Claim 'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn' is outdated/incorrect: Anthropic ships a native computer-use tool schema (computer_20241022, superseded by computer_20250124); if this skill wraps that API it should say so and pin the version

Claim 'Claude was trained on both' (element indices and coordinates) is inaccurate — Anthropic's computer-use training is coordinate/screenshot-based; Set-of-Mark indexing is a third-party prompting technique (originally for GPT-4V), so the rationale for index-clicking is stale even if the advice is sound

The documented tool interface (capture modes som/vision/ax, element-index clicks, capture_after=True) matches no public stable API; the doc names no repo, package, or version for the underlying implementation, making drift and breakage undetectable — likely a custom/internal wrapper that should be named and versioned
No dates, changelog, or 'last verified' stamp anywhere in the body; unversioned model references ('GPT', 'Gemini', 'open model via OpenAI-compatible endpoint') age poorly
Cannot audit links — frontmatter was stripped; any canonical doc/repo links should be checked for rot and re-verified

The 'universal, any-model' framing glosses over real differences in OpenAI's computer-use-preview and Gemini computer use offerings; 'any tool-capable model' should be qualified (e.g., vision-capable requirement for som/vision modes)
Only first 2000 chars of body provided; full document and the 5 references/ files could not be independently verified despite the 'verified present' claim
Fleet implementation status markers (e.g., '✅ Live' gaps closed Jul 4, 2026) are highly volatile content that goes stale faster than the Aug 2026 review date implies
Review timestamp (Aug 2026) freshness cannot be confirmed against the actual current date; if significant time has elapsed, subsystem status claims should be re-verified
No external URLs present so no dead-link risk, but internal relative paths (references/*.md) are unresolvable from the excerpt alone

All three referenced tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, OpenAI Codex CLI @openai/codex, OpenCode) are active, actively maintained projects as of latest knowledge — no deprecated or dead tools referenced in the umbrella itself
Cannot verify the three linked reference files (references/claude-code.md, codex.md, opencode.md) from this excerpt; CLI-specific details are where staleness usually accumulates

No last-reviewed date or version anchors in the doc; these CLIs iterate fast (e.g., Codex's TypeScript-to-Rust rewrite and changing default models/approval flags, Claude Code's evolving print-mode/SDK surface), so subsystem details may drift silently

Codex CLI ambiguity risk: 'OpenAI Codex' also refers to the deprecated 2021-era Codex API product; the doc correctly disambiguates via the @openai/codex npm package, but the reference file should preserve that disambiguation
Internal cross-reference to hermes-agent skill cannot be validated for existence or freshness from this excerpt

Tool name mismatch: the trycua/cua project ships a package/CLI called 'cua', not 'cua-driver'; commands like 'cua-driver skills install' and the '~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver' path cannot be verified and look fabricated or from a fork that was renamed

Core capability claim is dubious: 'actions do NOT move the user's cursor' and 'opposite of pyautogui' contradicts how trycua/cua and most computer-use drivers actually work — they drive the real host cursor unless running against a VM; on macOS CGEvent/AX automation generally does move focus

Inaccurate model claim: 'Claude was trained on both' element indices and pixel coordinates is misleading — Anthropic's computer-use tooling is screenshot/coordinate-based, not Set-of-Mark element indices; the element-index workflow is a wrapper convention, not something Claude was trained on

Ambiguous 'Hermes' runtime references (Hermes computer_use workflow, 'Hermes autodetection') are nonstandard/unverifiable jargon that will not age well and confuse readers unfamiliar with this internal agent
Fragile setup instructions: pointing at or symlinking '~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver' depends on an undocumented directory layout that the upstream repo may change without notice

Single hard-coded GitHub link (github.com/trycua/cua) with no version pinning or changelog; the repo has been actively restructured (library/CLI/MCP naming has churned), so the doc risks silently drifting from upstream
Cross-model claims ('works with any tool-capable model... GPT, Gemini') are asserted without caveats about differing tool-calling reliability, which may mislead users of weaker open models
Core git patterns (merge/rebase conflict handling, regenerating lockfiles/generated files, neutral third-party arbitration) are current and show no deprecated usage in the excerpt.

Depends on environment-specific tooling that cannot be verified as current: 'hermes kanban show <task-id>', 'delegate_task', and 'kanban_create(title=..., assignee=..., parents=[...])' are not standard public tools; if any have been renamed or retired, the Prerequisites and 'Spawned neutral agent' sections break with no fallback documented (only the intent-source path has a commit-message fallback).
'delegate_task' does not match the subagent-spawn tool name in major public agent runtimes (e.g., Claude Code uses 'Task'); confirm the exact tool identifier for the target environment.

Review scope is limited: frontmatter was stripped and only the first 2000 chars of the body were provided, so the Procedure section and any links or deprecated patterns beyond the cutoff were not assessed; no URLs appear in the excerpt, so dead links cannot be confirmed or ruled out in the unseen portion.
